A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Diorama. Their complete main texts, references, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original SSDB and ScanNet experiments, component ablations, and qualitative scene-modeling results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds ACDC comparisons and a user preference study, alongside revised quantitative results.

M1.justification: The perception, retrieval, and pose-estimation pipeline, including GigaPose scale prediction, remains. The reported optimization schedule changes locally: v1 places collision penalization in the Space stage, whereas v2 assigns it to Refinement (Section 3.2 and Appendix A.6).

E1.justification: SSDB, ScanNet/Scan2CAD, internet images, and text-conditioned image coverage remain. The added ACDC comparison introduces its approximately 8,800 OmniGibson simulation objects as retrieval data, a limited addition to object-asset coverage rather than a new scene benchmark.

E2.justification: ACDC, previously only cited, becomes a directly evaluated comparator for complete scene modeling and architecture reconstruction (v2 Tables 1–2). The SSDB pose comparisons also add original DINO-based ZSP alongside the retained DINOv2 variants, GigaPose, and best-matching-view baseline.

E3.justification: V2 adds a system-level evaluation using ground-truth boxes and masks, excluding SSDB ground-truth retrieval shapes, and measuring scene accuracy, similarity, preference, cost, and runtime. Appendix B.1 specifies different retrieval libraries for ACDC and Diorama and a study using 48 randomly sampled images with shuffled question order. These are additional protocols, not replacements for all existing experiments.

E4.justification: The pose-backbone analysis expands to include original DINO, extending the existing comparison of DINOv2 and fine-tuned DINOv2. The staged optimization ablation is also reported under the revised stage definitions. Object-group, retrieval-count, and simultaneous-versus-staged optimization analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the performance results. V2's added user preference percentage also lacks uncertainty reporting; additional point estimates do not establish a changed statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds system-level ACDC results, including 85.1% preference for Diorama, and an ACDC architecture row. Existing results also change: Diorama's SSDB ground-truth-depth alignment accuracy rises from 0.33 to 0.37, while fine-tuned ZSP falls from 0.34 to 0.25, reversing their ranking. ScanNet instance-average accuracy changes from 5.87 to 6.66, but class-average accuracy falls from 3.55 to 3.33. Multiple ablation tables are revised; retrieval Table 3 remains numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.6 adds explicit weighted definitions of the four stage objectives, including e1 = 3ealign + esem and e4 = 5eplace + ecol, and formalizes the revised allocation of collision penalization. Existing correspondence, similarity, and individual penalty definitions remain; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the central claim of a zero-shot, open-world, modular system for holistic CAD-based scene modeling without end-to-end training. The new comparisons support this retained contribution rather than redefine it. Adding 'Indoor' to the title makes the already stated application scope explicit.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of the ACDC comparison: low alignment is attributed to retrieval mismatch and depth errors, computational advantages to fewer LLM calls, and support-placement shortcomings to physics-based optimization. The existing limitations concerning geometry, texture, occlusion, and RANSAC sensitivity remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 newly discloses an RTX 4090 GPU, stage-loss weights, ACDC configuration and mesh-extraction procedures, and user-study procedures. GPT-4o checkpoint information, prompts, rendering resolutions, and optimizer schedules were already supplied in v1; their retention or relocation is not new disclosure.

R1.justification: V2 prunes cited works, including FreeZe, SAM-6D, FoundationPose, ULIP, and PointCLIP, and refines the motivation around CAD annotations useful for robot learning. The principal research positioning remains. ACDC was already cited in v1, although its empirical role expands substantially.

P1.justification: V2 adds 'Indoor' to the title, renames System to Approach, condenses the pose explanation, and moves technical exposition between the main text and supplement. The SSDB narrative is reordered to foreground system and architecture evaluation, while the overall section hierarchy and much of the prose remain.

P2.justification: The experimental displays are substantially reorganized. V2 adds ACDC comparison figures and a system table, promotes architecture results from the appendix, splits ground-truth and estimated-depth pose results into separate tables, and redistributes internet-image and text-to-scene examples. Appendix tables and large figures are extensively repositioned among the method descriptions.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful direct evidence about complete scene modeling against ACDC and improves reproducibility through explicit optimization weights and comparison procedures. The gain is limited by unequal retrieval libraries and incomplete user-study reporting. Some interpretation also lags behind revised evidence: Table 5's ground-truth-architecture ablation now performs worse than the full system, while the discussion retains its optimistic characterization of improved components.
